Needs changes before merge.

This is a safety-tier review. The PR includes the wrapped-A post from parent PR #2342. The new refusal text and its three tests are correct. Two findings from the maintainer's parent review remain in this head.

Requested before merge:

1. **Make the wrapped golden test pass on Windows.** `crates/app/tests/microarc_test_part.rs:279` permits an absolute G93 F difference of 0.04. The maintainer reported `F209.668 != F209.79` at golden line 661, plus differences of 0.049, 0.414 and 0.749. See [the parent review](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2342#issuecomment-6948308756). This child has the same test file, byte for byte. The reported 0.122 difference still exceeds its allowance. The test passes here on Linux; that does not resolve the Windows failure. Remove the platform dependence or use a justified relative bound. Keep the independent feed and A-rate checks. Do not replace the golden with output from one platform alone. Carry the parent fix into this stack before merge.

2. **Restore G94 before a turning rapid.** `assets/posts/tormach.cps:891` writes a turning G0 without a G94 reset. At line 800, `motionFor` skips the reset when `aNext` is set. I reproduced this with the unmodified trial-merged post. A feed from X0/A0 to X10/A30, then a rapid to X20/A60, gives:

   ```text
   G93 G1 X10 Y0 Z0 A30 F12
   G0 X20 Y0 Z0 A60
   G94
   ```

   The reset comes after the rapid. Add it before the rapid and add a test for this sequence. This resolves the maintainer's open modal-state finding and makes the post match its decision record.

Local checks against upstream/main `3c3a586865caba0b5dd45b241ff3396a76963a14`:

- The trial merge is clean. App and post test targets build.
- All 122 selected Rust tests pass: `first_4axis_part` (4), `fourth_axis_pose` (9), `index_swing` (13), `microarc_test_part` (3), `recorded_post_streams` (5), `rotary_feed_cap` (11), `tormach_fourth_axis` (12), `tormach_post` (10), `tormach_wrapped_a` (11), `explain_tormach` (3), `g93_feed` (5), `recorded_streams` (12), `script_tormach` (11), and `tormach_rotary_travel` (3).
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- The site test file has 12 passes and one existing failure. `test_machine_and_post_are_the_shipped_ones` searches `posting.rs` for the machine name. I repeated the failure with upstream main's test. This PR does not change that source or assertion.
- The quick dry run selects 838 steps, including unrelated suites. I ran the affected suites listed above.

Mutation checks used temporary files outside the repository:

- Remove the A-rate time bound: RED. F598.962 replaces F4.
- Remove angle unwrapping: RED. A-179 replaces A181.
- Restore the unchanged post: both checks GREEN.
- Restore the parent post: both new remedy checks are RED; both travel-boundary controls stay GREEN. Restore the fix: all checks are GREEN. The refused +361 and -361 targets are never written.

Golden checks: I checked all 3,245 NC lines for finite words, A travel, positive feeds, feed modes and G94 at spindle stops. I independently sampled every wrapped turning feed in the part frame. The maximum sampled feed is 203.17537 mm/min against 203.2 mm/min. The maximum A rate is 360 deg/min, within floating-point precision. The changed recorded refusal correctly names the unsupported B30 tilt. These checks pass. They do not resolve the two findings above.

Notes: No UI files change. No dependency, build script, workflow or script changes. No GitHub runner was used. No repository code or golden was changed. The posted continuous program and hardware cut remain untested, as the body states.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed:

1. Windows-sensitive wrapped golden comparison. G93 feeds now use a 0.2% relative bound instead of an absolute 0.04. The golden is unchanged. `wrap_golden_allows_only_bounded_platform_rounding` pins the reported F209.668/F209.79 pair, representative larger spreads, and rejection controls at low and high feeds. The independent tip-feed and A-rate checks remain. Reverting the bound made the pin RED. Restoring it made the pin GREEN.
2. G94 before a turning rapid. The turning-rapid branch now resets G94 before G0. `g94_comes_back_before_a_turning_rapid_after_a_g93_feed` pins the exact feed/reset/rapid sequence and checks rapid modal state. Removing the reset made the pin RED. Restoring it made the pin GREEN.

New head: eba0e477d755c99ac5fbf7d61e6490f76445cfe8.

Linux checks passed. MicroARC: 3 tests. Wrapped A: 12 tests. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 589 steps, zero failures. Clippy for camcraft-app and camcraft-post, all targets with warnings denied, passed. Windows execution was not available.

Please re-review this head. The PR remains a draft.

Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This is a safety-tier review. The PR includes the wrapped-A post from parent PR #2342. Both earlier blocking findings are resolved.

- The G93 golden comparison uses a 0.2% relative bound against the smaller positive feed. The decision record explains this bound. The tests cover the reported Windows F209.668/F209.79 pair and reject excessive changes at low and high feeds. Independent trajectory-feed and A-rate tests remain.
- The turning-rapid branch restores G94 before G0. The new test checks the exact sequence and the modal state of every rapid.
- Both overtravel refusals name the wider-travel remedy. The tests confirm that the refused +361 and -361 targets are not written. Both travel-boundary controls pass.

Local results after a clean trial merge with upstream/main `c605e5687c9197ff667092f001f9383384e35d01`:

- `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --no-run` passes.
- All 144 selected Rust tests pass.
- App suites: `conformance` (7), `first_4axis_part` (4), `fourth_axis_pose` (9), `index_swing` (13), `microarc_test_part` (3), `posting` (17), `recorded_post_streams` (5), `rotary_feed_cap` (11), `tormach_fourth_axis` (12), `tormach_post` (10), and `tormach_wrapped_a` (12).
- Post suites: `cycle_hop` (7), `explain_tormach` (3), `g93_feed` (5), `recorded_streams` (12), `script_tormach` (11), and `tormach_rotary_travel` (3).
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- The site test file has 12 passes and one existing failure. `test_machine_and_post_are_the_shipped_ones` searches `posting.rs` for the machine name. I reproduced the same failure with current upstream main's test and source. This PR does not change that assertion or source.
- The quick dry run selects 843 steps, including unrelated suites. I ran the affected suites listed above.

I repeated four mutations in temporary files outside the repository:

1. Restore the absolute 0.04 feed bound: RED. The platform-rounding test fails. Restore the relative bound: GREEN.
2. Remove G94 before the turning rapid: RED. G0 appears before G94. Restore the reset: GREEN.
3. Remove the A-rate time bound: RED. F598.962 replaces F4. Restore the bound: GREEN.
4. Remove angle unwrapping: RED. A-179 replaces A181. Restore unwrapping: GREEN.

All 12 wrapped-A tests and the comparator test also pass in the external harness without mutations.

Golden checks: I audited all 3,245 NC lines for finite words, positive feeds, A travel, feed modes, and G94 before rapids and spindle stops. I sampled each of the 2,678 turning feeds at 256 intervals in the part frame. The maximum sampled feed is 203.17537 mm/min against 203.2 mm/min. The maximum A rate is 360 deg/min, within floating-point precision. The golden has no changes since the earlier reviewed head. The changed recorded refusal correctly names the unsupported B30 tilt.

Requested before merge: none.

Notes: No UI, dependency, build-script, workflow, or script files change. No GitHub runner was used. Windows execution was not available. The posted continuous program and hardware cut remain untested, as the body states. The body identifies the stack on #2342. No repository code or golden was changed during this review.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
